pos.personaBrief: UEFA 2008/09: 'the norm for Pep Guardiola's team to monopolise the ball' (505-700 passes a match); City ranked first in possession in all 10 seasons (70% in 2017/18), with possession seen as a consequence of positional play rather than the aim.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up from the goalkeeper on goal-kicks and in open play, salida lavolpiana and a back three against a two-man press (Coaches' Voice 2021, Spielverlagerung 2014), but he rejects passing with no purpose ('pass with clear intention') and buys keepers who can hit long, accurate passes.

est.personaBrief: Juego de posicion, 'the search for superiority', with occupied zones, wingers giving maximum width and planned rotations (Spielverlagerung 2014, 2018); a false nine and players dropping into the defensive line are part of the structure.

lar.personaBrief: 'Superiority in the center', with the interior corridors as the key spaces; wide areas are 'only used for isolations and cut-backs' (Bayern-Dortmund 2015), but Robben, Ribery, Sane and Sterling held maximum width to open the middle.

blo.personaBrief: Advanced pressing, a high line that risks offside and an immediate, aggressive counter-press in all three spells (UEFA 2009, Coaches' Voice 2021/2022); later City added a 4-4-2 mid or low block.

mar.personaBrief: The base is 'zonal marking instead of man marking', with the Barcelona press blocking passing lanes (Spielverlagerung 2014); Bayern's duelling and City's early 2017/18 press added man-oriented elements, without dedicated man-markers.

pla.personaBrief: 'I want to play the way I want': fixed principles imposed at every club, but the structure changes often, within a match (four shapes against Dortmund, 2015) and from one opponent to the next (back three against a two-man press, Stones moving up against physical sides).

res.personaBrief: He wants 'beautiful football' and an attacking side that dominates the ball even in finals (Rome 2009), and he rejects playing for a draw; he is also driven to win, so what counts is purposeful dominance rather than style for its own sake.

sis.personaBrief: Positional play is 'the number one factor' in a Guardiola team's success, with defined roles and a counter-press for everyone; the system builds one-on-one isolations for wingers like Robben and Ribery to win their duels.

jog.personaBrief: Technique in every role: rondo goalkeepers, full-backs chosen for receiving under pressure, passers like Stones and Laporte, and Busquets and Rodri as pivots; on top of that he demands intensity and an aggressive counter-press.

bas.personaBrief: At Barcelona he promoted Busquets and Pedro, and seven academy players started the 2009 final; City was built mainly through expensive signings (Walker, Ederson, Laporte), with academy players like O'Reilly coming in later.

lid.personaBrief: A 'modus operandi based on convictions' and authority over the squad (Toure dropped until he apologised, Hart frozen out, 'I'm from the old generation'), along with a 'motivated, united' dressing room and training that is 'purposeful and fun'.
